newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Stocks level seen influencing copper price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Stocks level seen influencing copper price.

text.p: Expectations of a drawdown in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks held in Singapore should lend early market support to the red metal later on Tuesday, metals dealers said.
Rumours of a re-emergence of China as strong buyers of copper have led to predictions that stocks will decline by as much as 25,000 tonnes this week.
The LME will release stocks data at 0900 GMT on Tuesday.
A large decrease could provide the drive to enable copper to test the US$2,400 level, dealers said.
However, some dealers have suggested that in the longer-term, the Chinese may hold more copper than they immediately need, leading eventually to hefty bouts of selling.
Low volumes coupled with some forward selling on Monday quashed any bid to elevate the copper price, leaving three-month metal $1 lower at US$2,367 a tonne, dealers said.

The less-than-dynamic trend in LME copper trading has been reflected in the Shanghai market, where copper futures opened on Tuesday down slightly in dull trading. "The Chinese certainly don't seem too excited," said a Sydney dealer.

Broker JB Were and Son puts 1996 Chinese copper consumption at 1.2 million tonnes against mine production of only 481,000. "The shortfall was met by imports in the form of concentrate, scrap blister and refined metal," Were said in a report.

However, the Chinese government holds a substantial but undisclosed stockpile of refined copper, called the strategic reserve, Were noted. "We believe much of the copper stockpiled by China in 1996 is still stockpiled," the broker said.
In total, the broker sees Chinese imports of refined metal reaching only about 150,000 tonnes this year.
